claims.text: Negative enthalpies of mixing for selected binary pairs drive chemical short-range order in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys.
SRO suppresses lattice thermal conductivity more strongly than a random solid solution.
The greater conductivity suppression arises from enhanced phonon scattering by SRO-correlated atomic clusters.
The proposed suppression requires the SRO correlation length to exceed the phonon mean free path.
W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf and Nb-Mo-Ta-W can form BCC solid-solution states with controllable chemical ordering.
The initial disordered state has a statistically random atomic distribution and high configurational entropy.
Annealing below the order-disorder transition can induce pair-specific SRO, including Cr-Hf correlations in W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf.
The proposed annealing can produce SRO without macroscopic phase separation or long-range ordering.
For the W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf composition, temperatures from 300 K to 1000 K lie below the calculated Cr-Hf order-disorder transition near 1080 K and retain nonzero Cr-Hf ordering.
Phase separation is kinetically inhibited throughout the proposed 300 K to 1000 K annealing regime.
Rapid quenching preserves the annealing-induced SRO state for subsequent measurement.
SRO produces nanoscale regions with distinct local composition.
The SRO-associated regions generate local lattice-strain fields that act as phonon-scattering centers.
SRO creates spatially correlated atomic-mass and force-constant fluctuations that differ from random substitutional disorder.
Mass and force-constant correlations scatter phonons especially effectively when the SRO correlation length matches dominant phonon wavelengths.
Enhanced SRO scattering reduces the phonon mean free path and therefore lattice thermal conductivity.
An SRO-annealed sample will have statistically significantly lower lattice thermal conductivity than an as-quenched disordered sample despite unchanged precipitation and grain-boundary states.
The magnitude and possibly the sign of the conductivity response can depend on phonon dispersion, SRO correlation length, thermal history, and SRO-induced changes in phonon group velocity.
Quenching W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf from 1200 K should produce a more disordered state than annealing it at 800 K, because 1200 K is above and 800 K is below the calculated Cr-Hf ordering transition near 1080 K.
Equal or greater thermal conductivity in the confirmed-SRO sample, with no detected secondary phases, would falsify the predicted SRO-induced conductivity suppression.
